question: What are the physical facility requirements and fees to obtain ICAB accreditation for an internet cafe or pisonet business?
reference_answer: Under ICAB regulations for Internet Cafes and Pisonet operations, operators must comply with mandatory ocular standards: 1) ISP contract/receipt; 2) Half-closed cubicles not exceeding 5 feet from the floor; 3) Lighting of at least 25 Lux (fluorescent/LED) or 50 Lux (incandescent); 4) Permanently fixed webcams; 5) Content filtering systems blocking pornography; 6) 12x18 inch warning sign prohibiting minors prior to 6:00 AM and beyond 9:00 PM; and 7) Separate toilets for over 30 units. The ICAB accreditation fee is PHP 100.00 for the first 10 computer units plus PHP 10.00 for each additional unit.

question: What are the requirements, fee per hectare, and processing time for a CPDO Zoning Certification in Davao City?
reference_answer: A Zoning Certification is issued by the CPDO Zoning Enforcement Division based on the Integrated Zoning Ordinance (2019–2028) to certify land-use classification. Requirements are: 1) Accomplished application form (1 original); 2) Certified True Copy of Title from the Registry of Deeds (1 photocopy); 3) Subdivision / Sketch Plan by a Geodetic Engineer (1 original); and 4) CTO Official Receipt. The fee is PHP 750.00 per hectare, and total administrative processing time is 3 Days, 6 Hours, and 50 Minutes.

question: What are the required blueprint submittals and fee formulas to secure an FSEC from the Bureau of Fire Protection?
reference_answer: The Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC) is required prior to securing an OCBO building permit to certify design plan compliance with the Fire Code of the Philippines (RA 9514). Applicants must submit three (3) complete sets of architectural, civil, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, electronics, sanitary, and fire protection design plans signed and sealed by professionals, along with the PRC licenses and estimated building values. Fees are: 1) Application Fee of PHP 200.00; and 2) Fire Code Construction Tax (FCCT) of 0.1% of the verified estimated value of materials and labor, capped at a maximum of PHP 50,000.00.

question: Under what structural conditions are FSCR, FSCCR, and FSMR required by the BFP, and who prepares them?
reference_answer: Under RA 9514 regulations, specialized fire safety technical reports are mandatory if a building or establishment is required to install any or a combination of: 1) Wet standpipe systems; 2) Automatic fire suppression systems (AFSS); or 3) Automatic fire detection and alarm systems (FDAS). The required reports are: Fire Safety Compliance Report (FSCR) prepared by the Engineer/Architect of record and Fire Safety Practitioner during design; Fire Safety Compliance and Commissioning Report (FSCCR) by the contractor upon turnover; and Fire Safety Maintenance Report (FSMR) by the building administrator during annual inspections.

question: When must a business or contractor secure a BFP Fire Safety Clearance for welding, cutting, and hot works?
reference_answer: Under the BFP Citizen's Charter, a Fire Safety Clearance for welding, cutting, and other hot work operations must be secured under two operational categories: 1) Per Project Duration for new construction or renovation projects, applied during construction after conducting a fire safety inspection; or 2) Annual Fire Safety Clearance for business establishments requiring daily repair, fabrication, or hot work maintenance due to the routine nature of their business operations.
